text: Do not mistake me, and think that I mean to recommend to you abject and criminal flattery: no; flatter nobody's vices or crimes: on the contrary, abhor and discourage them. But there is no living in the world without a complaisant indulgence for people's weaknesses, and innocent, though ridiculous vanities.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XVII, to his son, London, October 16, Old Style 1747
